parts.label: b
parts.display_text: Explain why a macroscopic gas that has expanded to fill the box is overwhelmingly unlikely to return spontaneously to just its original half of the box.

answer.text: The equilibrium macrostate has overwhelmingly more accessible microstates. The probability of all N independently distributed molecules being in the original half is (1/2)ᴺ, which is negligible for a macroscopic N, but not mathematically zero.

sup-9690687ab15d5eb9-q61:whole.hint: Translate “isothermal” into a statement about temperature, then consider what that means for an ideal gas’s internal energy.
notes: For an ideal gas in an isothermal process, ΔU = 0 and therefore Q = W using work done by the gas. A fixed amount obeys pV = constant.
No temperature change does not mean no heat transfer. Heat can enter during expansion to replace the energy transferred out as work.

sup-9690687ab15d5eb9-q62:whole.hint: Treat the gas as the system and mark the directions of heat and work before substituting numbers.
notes: With W positive for work done by the gas and Q positive into it, ΔU = Q − W. “Rejects heat” makes Q negative; compression makes W negative.
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends on temperature. An unchanged temperature does not by itself mean no heat or work transfer.

sup-9690687ab15d5eb9-q64:whole.hint: Work is connected to the change in volume. On a pressure–volume graph, look for the relevant area.
notes: Work done by a gas is W = ∫p dV; at constant pressure it becomes pΔV. Expansion gives positive work by the gas, compression negative.
The enclosed area of a complete cycle is net work, with its sign set by the direction around the cycle. Convert kPa, MPa, litres and any axis multipliers before calculating.

sup-9690687ab15d5eb9-q65:whole.hint: Draw the energy entering from the hot reservoir, the useful work and the energy rejected to the cold reservoir.
notes: Over a complete engine cycle ΔU = 0, so W = Q_hot − Q_cold and efficiency = W/Q_hot. Use energy per cycle or power consistently.
Only an ideal reversible Carnot engine reaches η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot. Both reservoir temperatures must be in kelvin; this gives an upper bound for a real engine.

sup-eba893cae175369f-w1:c.i.hint: Count the microscopic arrangements that fit the same overall conditions.
notes: For equally accessible microstates, a macrostate with more arrangements is more probable. Entropy is related to multiplicity by S = k ln Ω.
